problem: On long-horizon instruction-following tasks such as ALFRED, agents fed with detailed multi-sentence instructions still skip subtasks, interact with wrong objects, or wander after finishing a subtask. They lack explicit awareness of where they are in the subtask sequence and how far they have progressed within a subtask.
motivation: Subtasks in long-horizon tasks are sequentially dependent (e.g. heat the potato before placing it), so one missed subtask dooms the whole task. Implicit progress monitoring inside a single policy network (attention, hidden state) is unreliable, which motivates an explicit, grounded progress tracker.
key_idea: Extract a per-subtask milestone (type + target objects) from each low-level instruction with a BERT-CRF tagger, and ground it with a reachability-aware Mask R-CNN to decide when to advance the instruction and to proactively reject actions on wrong objects.
insight: Explicit, grounded progress monitoring beats implicit monitoring and learned binary completion classifiers. In the ablation, checking before execution (proactive) beats checking after execution (passive), and both beat a binary milestone classifier (e.g. VLN-BERT val-unseen SR 17.29 / 17.05 / 14.85). The 2x2 table shows the gain is largest when M-Track is used in both training and test. Error analysis shows that 'navigate to next subtask location' failures drop to 0 (from 101 for the LSTM), and that GT milestones give only a moderate further gain (24.38 SR), so the builder is already fairly accurate.
method: Milestone builder: BERT-CRF NER tagger with BIO tags labels each low-level instruction with (navigation|interaction, target objects). It is trained on labels derived from ALFRED PDDL annotations and frozen during agent training; it reaches F1 90-97. Instructions with no target are merged with the next one.
Milestone checker (state estimation): Mask R-CNN (ResNet-50-FPN) fine-tuned on ALFRED, with an extra binary head predicting whether each object is reachable (within 1.5 m).

Milestone checker (grounding): match target names to detected class labels via WordNet WUP similarity; an interaction milestone additionally requires the predicted object mask to have IoU > 0.5 with the grounded target. A checklist handles multiple targets, and a milestone is skipped after 15 consecutive failures.
Instruction feeding: give the agent only the high-level goal plus the current low-level sentence, and advance to the next sentence only once the milestone is reached.

Proactive action checking: reject a predicted interaction whose mask does not match the milestone target and try the next of the top-N=5 (action, mask) candidates. If none matches, fall back to the top navigation action.

Base agents: Enhanced VLN-BERT (recurrent VLN-BERT with 8 panoramic scene features, 20 object features, and a pointer network over navigation/interaction/stop) and an Enhanced Seq2Seq-LSTM. Both use an ALFRED-pretrained Mask R-CNN and are trained with behavior cloning plus A2C, using distance, interaction-match, visibility and final-success rewards.

setting.backbone: VLN-BERT (adapted, trained) and CNN-LSTM with BERT language encoder (trained), plus BERT-CRF milestone tagger and Mask R-CNN detector
setting.training_data: ALFRED training split only (21,023 examples), including panoramic ground-truth trajectories generated by the ALFRED augmentation tool; Mask R-CNN and BERT-CRF are trained on labels from ALFRED metadata/PDDL; VLN-BERT initialized from R2R-pretrained weights
setting.observation: egocentric RGB with 8 panoramic views (4 headings x 2 elevations) plus detected objects and reachability
setting.action_space: ALFRED discrete: 5 navigation actions, 7 interaction actions with an object mask, and Stop
setting.privileged: none at test time for the main results (the GT-milestone variant is an ablation upper bound only)

results: M-Track improves unseen test SR of the enhanced LSTM from 8.70 to 13.28 and of the enhanced VLN-BERT from 12.23 to 16.29 (about 52% and 33% relative). VLN-BERT+M-Track matches the best published method HLSM on unseen SR (16.29) and has higher unseen PLWSR (7.66 vs 4.34).
limitations: Assumes the instruction is divisible into subtask-aligned sentences with explicit object targets; implicit milestones (e.g. 'fetch a cold beer') are not handled.
Milestones are hard constraints and checking is declarative on the environment state, so it fails for procedural instructions ('turn around twice') or multiple valid subtask orders.
Weak on multi-interaction tasks (Heat & Place 19% completion on val unseen), and seen-environment results trail the best published methods.
